name: Transient route → RETRY: transient failure, grace remains → re-dispatch Amelia (free of the convergence budget)
description:
The transient-retry route (adopt-reason-aware-escalate, #529/#569). When a developer loop failed for a TRANSIENT reason (route.attempt.transient="true" — the check_floors ATOMIC-MIRROR classification of the loop's harness-stamped agent.loop.terminal-reason ∈ {model_error, handler_error}, stamped in the SAME ReplaceTriples as route.attempt.passed) AND the attempt was NOT clean (route.attempt.unclean="true", the 06b/06e OR-collapse — passed=false OR a floor rejected) AND the transient-retry grace still has room (route.transient.instance count < CAP=2), re-dispatch a FRESH developer loop — WITHOUT consuming the convergence attempt budget. A flaky endpoint must not exhaust a task's convergence budget: on_enter appends task.transient.instance (the SEPARATE transient counter), NOT task.attempt.instance, so route.attempt.instance (the budget count) is unchanged. If the retried loop then succeeds → advance (06a); if it fails GENUINELY → the convergence routes (06c/06d) take over on the untouched budget; if it fails transiently again → the transient count rises toward the cap (06g parks).

★ WHY THE CLASSIFICATION IS IN THE MIRROR, NOT A RULE: the engine executes each rule action as its OWN graph mutation (one KV revision per add_triple) and evaluates per debounce-flush against freshly-fetched state — so a rule-stamped transient collapse lands in a SEPARATE revision from 06b's unclean stamp, and 06c's exclusion RACES it (the double-dispatch caught live by TestBridgeProofTransientGraceRetries). Route mutual exclusion is only sound as a CONDITION PARTITION over one atomic snapshot; the mirror's single ReplaceTriples is that snapshot. route.attempt.transient is therefore ALWAYS present ("true"/"false") wherever any floors-route condition is satisfiable.

⚠ SERIALIZATION INVARIANT: this rule joins dispatch-developer (04), floors-retry (06c), and review-retry (07b) as a SANCTIONED role=developer spawner (pinned — one developer in flight per task). It fires on a TERMINATED loop's terminal and is self-extinguishing, so exactly one developer loop is ever in flight.

TRIGGER = the developer loop L_n: route.attempt.transient eq "true" AND route.attempt.unclean eq "true" AND route.transient.instance length_lt 2 (required:true — the transient grace cap; a LITERAL, so an absent counter is a valid 0 = the first transient failure, no fail-open) AND route.attempt.routed length_eq 0 (self-extinguish). Mutually exclusive with the transient-park (06g, length_gte 2) on the transient count, and with the convergence routes (06c/06d exclude via route.attempt.transient eq "false" — the same atomic flag, opposite value).

★ WHY THE GATE IS unclean, NOT passed=false (route TOTALITY): the mirror stamps passed/rejected/transient INDEPENDENTLY, so the cell passed=true ∧ rejected=true ∧ transient=true is reachable (measured green, a structural floor rejected the artifact, then the loop's final model call died transiently). A passed=false gate leaves that cell UNROUTED — 06a needs rejected=false, 06c/06d are transient-excluded — a permanent silent stall (caught in adversarial review). unclean covers exactly the not-advance region, so 06c ∪ 06d ∪ 06f ∪ 06g ⊇ unclean (the 8-cell totality census pins it). Race-safe: unclean is only the SHARED TRIGGER — a late-landing unclean delays this route a pass; it cannot split the partition, which lives on the ATOMIC mirror flag. A measured-green rejected=false loop still advances via 06a (unclean never stamped).

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe, CRITICAL): on_enter FIRST stamps route.attempt.routed=$entity.instance on L_n, guarded by route.attempt.routed length_eq 0, BEFORE the publish. publish_agent is NOT idempotent — a re-fire would spawn a DUPLICATE developer. A fresh loop per re-dispatch re-arms it.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.developer
on_enter.prompt:
SEMDEV DEVELOPER (Amelia) — your previous attempt on this run's task was interrupted by a TRANSIENT infrastructure error (the model or a tool endpoint failed), NOT by a problem with your work. There is nothing to fix from that interruption — just proceed with the task.

Your run entity ID is $entity.triple.agent.run.entity-id. Read the task contract and any prior recorded measurement/floor findings with query_entity(entity_id="$entity.triple.agent.run.entity-id"); read the files with read_workspace. Author (or continue) the fix touching only task.spec.target-files with apply_patch, then measure_task(task_index=0). Iterate until the test passes, then stop. You author the fix; the harness measures it and you never claim the outcome (G3).

metadata.station: transient retry — transient failure + grace remains → re-dispatch Amelia free of the convergence budget (adopt-reason-aware-escalate)
metadata.serialization_invariant: this rule + dispatch-developer (04) + floors-retry (06c) + review-retry (07b) are the ONLY sanctioned role=developer spawners (pinned) — one developer in flight per task.
metadata.transient_flag: route.attempt.transient is the check_floors MIRROR classification (always "true"/"false", atomic with route.attempt.passed in one ReplaceTriples) — NOT a rule-stamped collapse; a rule-stamped sibling lands in a separate KV revision and the convergence routes race it (the pinned double-dispatch).
metadata.transient_budget: route.transient.instance length_lt 2 (a LITERAL cap, so absent = 0 = first transient failure, no fail-open). Partitions the transient count with 06g's length_gte 2 (no gap, no overlap).
metadata.not_budget: on_enter appends task.transient.instance (NOT task.attempt.instance) — a transient re-dispatch does NOT consume the convergence budget.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via route.attempt.routed (shared, LOOP-scoped) stamped BEFORE the publish — CRITICAL (publish_agent is not idempotent).
